title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 23
summary: It is Day 23 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - JANUARY 11: Dez Bryant #88 of the Dallas Cowboys attempts a catch over Sam Shields #37 of the Green Bay Packers during the 2015 NFC Divisional Playoff game at Lambeau Field on January 11, 2015 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Initially ruled a catch, the call was reversed upon review. (Photo by Mike McGinnis/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 23 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Welcome for Day 23 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the most controversial and painful playoff defeats in Cowboys history. Yes, it’s the much famed “Dez Caught It” game. Sunday, January 11, 2015 — 1:05 p.m. ET Lambeau Field, Green Bay, Wisconsin Final Score: Green Bay Packers 26, Dallas Cowboys 21 The matchup carried considerable historical weight. Dallas and Green Bay had both finished the regular season 12-4, with the Cowboys winning all eight of their road games and the Packers going undefeated at Lambeau Field. Green Bay struck first when Aaron Rodgers found Andrew Quarless for a four-yard touchdown. Dallas answered with a long, methodical drive that ended with Tony Romo throwing a one-yard scoring pass to fullback Tyler Clutts, tying the game at 7-7. The Cowboys moved ahead after Jeremy Mincey forced and recovered a Rodgers fumble. Romo capitalized by hitting Terrance Williams on a short pass that Williams turned into a 38-yard touchdown, giving Dallas a 14-7 lead. The Cowboys had an opportunity to extend that advantage before halftime, but Dan Bailey’s 50-yard field-goal attempt was blocked. Rodgers then quickly moved Green Bay into position for Mason Crosby’s 40-yard field goal as time expired, reducing Dallas’ lead to 14-10. One of the game’s biggest swings arrived early in the third quarter. DeMarco Murray broke through the line with open space ahead of him, but Julius Peppers knocked the ball loose and Green Bay recovered. Crosby converted a 30-yard field goal from the turnover, bringing the Packers within one point. Dallas responded with an 80-yard drive capped by Murray’s one-yard touchdown run, restoring a 21-13 advantage. Green Bay’s offense then found its rhythm. Rodgers connected with rookie Davante Adams for a 46-yard touchdown late in the third quarter, cutting the margin to 21-20. After the Packers forced a punt, Rodgers completed seven consecutive passes on an 80-yard drive and found Richard Rodgers for a 13-yard score. Green Bay failed on the two-point conversion but still moved ahead 26-21. Dallas received one final opportunity with less than five minutes remaining. Facing fourth-and-two from the Green Bay 32-yard line, Romo gave Bryant a chance against single coverage. Bryant climbed over Sam Shields, secured the ball, took multiple steps and stretched toward the goal line before the ball moved as he contacted the ground. The play was initially ruled a catch at the Packers’ one-yard line. Mike McCarthy challenged the ruling, and referee Gene Steratore overturned it. Under the catch rule in place at the time, officials determined Bryant had not maintained control throughout the process of going to the ground. The reversal produced a turnover on downs with 4:06 remaining, and Dallas never regained possession as Green Bay converted two third downs and exhausted the clock. This game belongs on the countdown because it became much larger than the final score. The Cowboys had completed a 12-win regular season, captured the NFC East and won a playoff game for the first time since the 2009 season. They then went into Lambeau Field and stood inches from potentially taking the lead against one of the NFC’s strongest teams. Instead, their season ended on a ruling that Cowboys fans continue to debate today. #Cowboys vs #Packers 2014 Divisional Round Final Score: Green Bay Packers 26, Dallas Cowboys 21 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/GIh1QjoPr8 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 21, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game NFL owners unanimously approved a simplified catch rule in 2018 that removed the old requirement to maintain possession throughout the process of going to the ground. The league specifically cited Bryant’s overturned reception as the type of play that would be treated as a catch under the revised standard. title: Malik Davis will try to secure Cowboys’ RB2 job this week
summary: Most of the conversation around the Dallas Cowboys running back depth this offseason has centered around both of their second-year running backs Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah. Most of the conversation heading into the Cowboys second game of the preseason is now centered around fourth-year running back Malik Davis. While Davis may lack some of […]
full_text: Most of the conversation around the Dallas Cowboys running back depth this offseason has centered around both of their second-year running backs Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah. Most of the conversation heading into the Cowboys second game of the preseason is now centered around fourth-year running back Malik Davis. While Davis may lack some of the flash that a player like Jaydon Blue possesses, or some of the Marshawn Lynch-type runs that a player like Phil Mafah brings, what Davis brings to the table is consistency, and that’s something we have not seen yet from any of the young backs. Davis was a UDFA for the Cowboys after the 2022 NFL draft. In 12 games with the team, Davis rushed 38 times for 161 yards (4.2 yards per carry) and a touchdown. Davis did not see action in 2023 and was later waived, but was re-signed to the practice squad, which is where he spent time for the remainder of the 2023 season and the entire 2024 season. Davis was waived two times in 2025, before finally getting an opportunity on the active roster. After seeing action in 10 games in 2025, Davis finished the season with 52 carries for 250 yards (4.8 yards per carry) and two touchdowns. Similar to what he did in 2023, Davis kept his head down, worked his way onto the field, and impressed when given an opportunity, and what do you know, that’s pretty much the same thing that is happening right now. Heading into Oxnard, Davis was merely an afterthought. With many expecting a big jump from Jaydon Blue and/or Phil Mafah, Davis was not viewed as an option for the Cowboys 53-man roster, but with two preseason games left, and with Blue and Mafah both being limited in practices with injuries, the former Florida running back is now in the mix to not only make the Cowboys final roster, but he has a great case for winning the RB2 job behind starter Javonte Williams. With Blue and Mafah likely limited for the Cowboys week two preseason game against the Cardinals, Davis will likely see a heavy workload, along with Israel Abanikanda. It’s hard not to root for Davis given how much adversity he’s had to deal with in his short NFL career. For a player that tends to show up every time his number is called, it’s hard to believe he has yet to stick around and earn a spot in the NFL. With just a few weeks left until 53-man roster cutdowns, Davis has an inside track to making the final roster for the Cowboys, and possibly play a relatively big role in the process. Who do you think will end up with the RB2 role heading into the season? Hit the comments and let us know.

RICHARDSON (Photo By Helen H. Richardson/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys made a bit of history with their preseason win last week. To be clear, wins and losses in the preseason are hardly the most important thing, but winning is obviously cooler than losing. By beating the Seattle Seahawks the Cowboys started off a preseason 1-0 and did so for the first time since 2017. It really is amazing that in almost a decade this never happened. Well there is another potential point of history to fall should the team win this week. Starting the preseason off 1-0 means that the Cowboys have the potential to double their win total with a 2-0 start. Do you know when the last time was that the Cowboys were 2-0 to start the preseason? It’s been even longer. It was in 2007 when the Cowboys beat the Denver Broncos (after beating the Indianapolis Colts in the preseason opener) that the franchise was last 2-0 in the preseason. Look at these photos! The 2007 season in general was among the more magical throughout the duration of The Drought™ so it is always nice to see it brought to the front of conversation. Perhaps the Cowboys will have a similar level of success this season should they start this preseason off 2-0 as well.

After starting their preseason slate with an impressive performance against the Seattle Seahawks, Dallas will face another NFC West opponent this Saturday, traveling to Arizona to take on the Cardinals. The second preseason game tends to carry significant weight in determining what players ultimately make the 53-man roster. With that thought in mind, today we take a look at three offensive players with the most to prove on Saturday night in Arizona. 1) RB Jaydon Blue To this point, Jaydon Blue’s Cowboys tenure has been disappointing, to say the least. After playing in just five games during his rookie year, Blue looked to take a step forward this year and cement himself as Dallas’ RB2 in Oxnard. So far, that has not happened. While he has shown some flashes during camp, Blue has struggled with consistency, and his fumbling habits have reared their ugly head once again. In Dallas’ first preseason game against Seattle, Blue got the most carries of any Cowboys running back, but the 22-year-old was not productive. The former Texas Longhorn recorded just 19 yards on eight carries, an average of 2.4 Y/A on the day. To make matters worse, Blue hurt his shoulder during the game, forcing him to not participate in the scrimmage against the New Orleans Saints on Tuesday. Blue’s availability for Saturday night is still up in the air, but if he does play, there may be no Cowboy on the roster with more to prove in Arizona. Time is running out for the young running back to prove he is capable of being RB2. If he wants a real chance to secure the job, it has to start with a good performance on Saturday night. 2) QB Joe Milton Cowboys’ quarterback Joe Milton’s preseason got off to a fantastic start. While he did not start the game, the 26-year-old signal caller completed 12 of 15 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown. Following Milton’s productive performance, the Cowboys have not announced which quarterback will start on Saturday night in Arizona. All things considered, Dallas would likely prefer Milton to show he is capable of being their backup quarterback. While Sam Howell has more NFL starting experience, Milton is the higher-ceiling player at the position. Given Dak Prescott’s advanced age, the Cowboys need a plan in place if he goes down with an injury this season. At this point, Milton may have more bust potential, but he also is capable of doing things athletically and arm-wise that Howell is not. If the former sixth-round pick can build upon his performance from last week against the Cardinals, there is a good chance he could take a firm lead in the race for the backup quarterback spot. 3) WR Jonathan Mingo Much like Jaydon Blue, Jonathan Mingo’s Cowboys tenure has not featured many highlights. Mingo came into camp with plenty to prove if he wanted to make the final 53-man roster. While he wasn’t the star on Saturday night, the 25-year-old’s arrow appears to be trending up after a solid showing against the Seahawks. Mingo caught two passes for 20 yards to go with an impressive effort play on special teams. If Jonathan Mingo makes the 53-man roster, it will be because of plays like this. A solid night, on top of a special teams effort play like this goes a long way. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/DGSJXTzQi5 — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) August 16, 2026 If Mingo makes the 53, his ability to make an impact on special teams will likely be a big factor. He showed he is fully capable of doing just that on Saturday night. For arguably the first time during his tenure as a Cowboy, the former second-round pick has a chance to build upon a solid performance and help continue to make a case for why he deserves to make the final 53.

title: Cowboys OLB Von Miller impresses in first practice with team
summary: Dallas Cowboys fans have been begging for Von Miller for what seems like decades. Heading into the 2026 season, that dream is now a reality. After weeks of romance on social media from the future Hall of Famer, the Cowboys announced on Sunday night that Miller will be wearing a star in 2026. Miller arrived […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - AUGUST 18: Dallas Cowboys linebacker Von Miller waves to fans following a joint training camp practice with the New Orleans Saints on Tuesday, Aug. 18, 2026, in Oxnard, Calif. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images) Dallas Cowboys fans have been begging for Von Miller for what seems like decades. Heading into the 2026 season, that dream is now a reality. After weeks of romance on social media from the future Hall of Famer, the Cowboys announced on Sunday night that Miller will be wearing a star in 2026. Miller arrived in Oxnard on Wednesday and spoke to the media for the first time before the Cowboys joint practice with the New Orleans Saints. It’s been mentioned multiple times since the signing about what Miller will bring to the locker room as a teammate, culture builder, and mentor to Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence. But in the Cowboys last practice in Oxnard, the media in attendance were able to get a first-hand look at what Miller will be brining to the field for the Christian Parker led defense in 2026. Miller saw very limited work in the team drills on Thursday (no video permitted during team drills), but he took advantage of the few opportunities he got in his first practice with the Cowboys. According to Nick Harris of the Star Telegram, Miller played four snaps in the team portion of practice and had a pressure against Terence Steele on his first rep. Clarence Hill Jr. of DLLS Cowboys, also reported that Miller had two pressures during team period against Steele and also “bulldozed” Nate Thomas on another rep. Von Miller still has something in the tank. He beat Terence Steele for two pressures in Dak Prescott He bulldozed Nate Thomas pic.twitter.com/W42C5TGUeG — Clarence Hill Jr (@clarencehilljr) August 20, 2026 The Cowboys do not need Miller to play 40-50 snaps a game. They brought him in to make an impact in obvious pass situations, and from the looks of his first practice with the Cowboys, he’s still able to do that at a pretty high level. Miller will unlikely see any action in the preseason, so we will have to wait for the Cowboys to return to Frisco before we get more updates on Miller’s play on the field, but the early (and limited) return on the Miller signing seems to be all positive in his first week in Dallas.

title: Cowboys news: Final practices in Oxnard finished before heading to Arizona
summary: It feels like just yesterday all Dallas Cowboys fans were anticipating the team’s arrival in Oxnard, California for training camp. After just under a month in Oxnard, the Cowboys finished their final real practice as they turn their attention to their week two preseason game. After a nice game one win against the defending Super […]
full_text: It feels like just yesterday all Dallas Cowboys fans were anticipating the team’s arrival in Oxnard, California for training camp. After just under a month in Oxnard, the Cowboys finished their final real practice as they turn their attention to their week two preseason game. After a nice game one win against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, the Cowboys will travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals Saturday night. With plenty of roster decisions to be made, let’s take a look at how the final practice in Oxnard in 2026 went. Practice Points: Nearing the end in Oxnard – DallasCowboys.com Team portion of the Cowboys final “open” practice in Oxnard did not allow video. But the mothership staff still got a first-hand look at the Cowboys team portion of practice. Here are some observations: Hard to Run: Thursday’s final training camp practice in Oxnard was a good one for Dallas’ run defense, which continued to make things difficult at the line of scrimmage. Donovan Ezeiruaku having a tackle for loss and DJ Withers having a run stuff on Israel Abanikanda were two of the big plays that stood out, but the defense as a whole was able to plug up the middle well as they’ve done for a majority of camp, albeit difficult to figure out truly how good a run defense is until live tackling is allowed in a game setting. – (Tommy Yarrish) NFL FINES COWBOYS, SAINTS $500K EACH FOR UNSPORTSMANLIKE BEHAVIOR AT JOINT PRACTICE – NFL.com The NFL announced the Cowboys and Saints would be fined $500K each for the fight filled joint practice on Wednesday. With that large of a fine, let’s hope both teams got their money’s worth. The NFL confirmed on Thursday that it has fined the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints organizations $500,000 after there were multiple fights during a joint practice session on Tuesday in Oxnard, California. “The Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints have each been fined $500,000 for the actions that took place at the joint practice between the teams earlier this week,” the league said in a statement. “The Competition Committee has made sportsmanship — including at joint practices — a point of emphasis over the past several years. All clubs were reminded by memo prior to training camp of their responsibility in preventing unsportsmanlike behavior at joint practices that has the potential to result in injury.” Cowboys injury updates: James Houston, Jay Toia exit Thursday’s practice – RJ Ochoa, Blogging the Boys The Cowboys have remained relatively healthy throughout their time in Oxnard in 2026. That being said, they had multiple players leave practice early on Thursday. The Dallas Cowboys are putting the finishing touches on the Oxnard portion of training camp on Thursday, and unfortunately it was not a fully clean effort in that regard. It was reported early in the afternoon that defenders James Houston and Jay Toia each took to the injury tent at different points in time. You never want to see that. 10 Dallas Cowboys who exceeded Brian Schottenheimer’s expectations during team’s training camp stay in Oxnard – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Dallas Cowboys’ head coach Brian Schottenheimer gave a list of players that stood out in training camp. There’s a few interesting names currently in some heated position battles still to be decided. And while the preseason is far from over, head coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked to name the five players that exceeded his expectations during the team’s time in the West Coast. In true Schottenheimer fashion, we wasn’t able to stop at five. So he named ten. DB Caleb Downs ED Rashan Gary DL Otito Ogbonnia CB Shavon Revel Jr. WR Jonathan Mingo WR Camden Brown LT Tyler Guyton RB Javonte Williams WR Ryan Flournoy P Bryan Anger What’s encouraging to Brian Schottenheimer as Cowboys close out California portion of camp? – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News Brian Schottenheimer was very encouraged at what he saw in Oxnard. Carrying that encouragement into the regular season, and better yet, into the postseason is the major question. “We’re still very much in the training camp mode,” he said before a nearly two-hour practice Thursday. “Training camp will last about another 10 days. Even when we leave Oxnard, we’re still in training camp mode. We’re still putting in the last two installs. So [Thursday’s] install number eight, third-down day. And then we’ll get to install nine when you get back to Frisco and back home. But expect these guys to do a great job like they always do with cracks and playing with good pad level, protecting each other. But should be a very spirited day.” The Good & Not So Good From Final Dallas Cowboys Training Camp Practice in Oxnard – Randy Gurzi, SI.com One of the biggest questions coming into training camp was what should the Cowboys expect from Tyler Guyton? With Oxnard practices coming to an end, it sounds like Guyton may finish as one of the biggest winners of training camp. Good: Tyler Guyton is impressing Tyler Guyton entered the offseason as a question mark for the Cowboys but has been far more impressive than anticipated. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer praised him for his work during camp and he followed with another strong performance, even being singled-out by Patrik Walker for his work during camp. Tyler Guyton is having the best camp of his young #Cowboys career. https://t.co/wrPdvvc17W — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) August 19, 2026 Daily discussion question: What is the main thing you want to see on Saturday night?

title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 33-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers
summary: Well, that was ugly. The Denver Broncos’ preseason winning streak has ended after the Packers dominated them tonight. However, the Broncos still end the night as winners due to Bo Nix and Jaylen Waddle looking good and making an impact when they were on the field. At the end of the day, that is all […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) passes in the first quarter during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Well, that was ugly. The Denver Broncos’ preseason winning streak has ended after the Packers dominated them tonight. However, the Broncos still end the night as winners due to Bo Nix and Jaylen Waddle looking good and making an impact when they were on the field. At the end of the day, that is all that matters from this game. With that said, here are my winners and losers from the Broncos’ 33-13 loss to the Packers in Week 2 of the preseason. WINNER – Bo Nix Bo Nix is BACK! The Broncos quarterback took the field for the first time since suffering a broken ankle vs. the Buffalo Bills in the Divisional Round of the playoffs and played very well. He led the Broncos to a touchdown drive in his opening drive and connected with Jaylen Waddle for a big 35-yard gain during the drive. Nix finished the night going 6 of 9 for 76 yards and 1 touchdown. BO NIX TOUCHDOWN TO RJ HARVEY pic.twitter.com/28bMlSzQ6h — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 22, 2026 This is what we needed to see. Nix looked healthy, locked in, and ready for the regular-season opener vs. the Chiefs. We’ll see if he plays in the preseason finale, but I have seen enough and wouldn’t mind if he rested until Week 1. WINNER – Jaylen Waddle Jaylen Waddle hit the field for the first time in a Denver Broncos uniform, and he did not disappoint. Waddle got open in the middle of the field, Nix found him and hit him for a 35-yard catch-and-run. Get used to this, Broncos Country; we are going to see it a lot moving forward. Jaylen Waddle 🐧🐧 pic.twitter.com/86Xeb4XRfG — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 22, 2026 Waddle looked healthy after sitting out a week or so during training camp with a soft tissue injury, which is great to see. He looked quick, healthy, and like the playmaker the Broncos traded for. Like Nix, I have seen enough, and we’ll see you in Week 1 when the games start to count. LOSER – Jarrett Stidham After promising preseason opening performance, Jarrett Stidham had a rough showing vs. the Packers. He finished the night 9 of 15 for 82 yards, 0 touchdowns, and 1 bad interception. While his handle of the backup job may not be in danger, he did not look very good tonight. The positive for him was that he was the second quarterback up again tonight despite splitting time with Sam Ehlinger with the 2s throughout camp. That is a sign that he is the leader for the backup quarterback job, which seemed like the likely outcome regardless. However, you hoped to see a better performance from Stidham, who lost the confidence of some of the fan base after his performance in the AFC Championship Game. LOSER – Broncos defense After a strong showing in Week 1 vs. the Falcons, the Broncos had some struggles vs. the Packers. The starting defense showed some flashes, but still gave up an opening-drive touchdown to Jordan Love, who connected with MarShawn Lloyd From there, the Packers’ second – and third-string offenses dominated the Broncos’ reserves throughout the remainder of the game. They could not stop their run game, and both their backup and third-string quarterbacks had success. There were some bright spots, but overall, not the best showing for the Broncos defense, which has been pretty solid up until tonight. Good tape and teaching moments for Vance Joseph and his unit. WINNER – RJ Harvey While Harvey may not be the best pure runner on the team, what he can do in the passing game is, what Sean Payton would say, his superpower. He ran a wheel route down the sideline, and Nix threw a beautiful pass to him for an opening-drive touchdown by the offense. This is where Harvey is going to excel. He could catch 50 or 60 passes this season and be an impact player in space and in the passing game. Dobbins and Coleman will likely handle the majority of the work in the run game, with Harvey filtering in from time to time, but again, he will thrive as a pass catcher. Other notable winners and losers WINNER – WR Pat Bryant: He got the start alongside Waddle and Sutton and has all but locked down the WR3 role. WINNER – RB Jonah Coleman: He came in after RJ Harvey, played, I believe, one series, and was out of the game. His limited usage in the preseason shows what the team feels about him, and that is a great sign. WINNER – EDGE Que Robinson: He had a nifty pass rush move and a sack. He was pressuring the QB throughout, and despite an iffy roughing-the-passer call, he had a great night. LOSER – Injuries: Starting corner Riley Moss left the game with a rib injury during the opening drive of the game and did not return. Not what you want to see. LOSER – Broncos reserve OL: They struggled to pass block and to get anything going in the run game. Not a great night for the Broncos reserve offensive line. LOSER – Penalties: Broncos had 10 penalties for 79 yards and what seemed like a holding call every time they ran the ball late in the game. Not what you want to see. LOSER – Special Teams : They gave up some big returns in the kicking game. WINNER – LB Karene Reid: He came in after the starters and made some plays. Sure seems like he’s a favorite for a spot on the 53-man roster once again this season. LOSER – Preseason win streak: The Broncos’ preseason win streak that dated back a couple of years ended tonight. LOSER – Overall play: The Packers simply outplayed the Broncos in all three phases for the most part tonight. The starters did alright, but after that, it was rough.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Instant reaction: Broncos throttled by Packers in second preseason game
summary: The Denver Broncos had won eight preseason games in a row with Head Coach Sean Payton at the helm. Alas, tonight that streak wended. When the clock struck zero, the Broncos suffered a 33-13 defeat to the Green Bay Packers. Here are several instant reactions from their first preseason game. Welcome back, Bo Nix! Broncos […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 21: Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on in the first half of a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Tyler Schank/Clarkson Creative/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos had won eight preseason games in a row with Head Coach Sean Payton at the helm. Alas, tonight that streak wended. When the clock struck zero, the Broncos suffered a 33-13 defeat to the Green Bay Packers. Here are several instant reactions from their first preseason game. Welcome back, Bo Nix! Broncos Country waited a long time for quarterback Bo Nix to get back on the football field. Even though it was a brief preseason debut, it was great to see Denver’s high-caliber signal caller on the field. In limited action, I thought Nix looked good. On their first offensive possession, the Broncos embarked on a six play, 65-yard drive. A 35-yard strike to Jaylen Waddle put the Broncos in scoring position. A few players later, a beautiful 21-yard throw by Nix to RJ Harvey that evened the score at 7-7. Divvying up the ball to a variety of targets, Nix looked poised in the pocket and comfortable on the move. Early on in the second quarter, Nix was replaced by Jarrett Stidham after the offense’s second drive of the game resulted in a 53-yard field goal by Wil Lutz. In his two possessions, Nix went 6-of-9 for 79 yards and 1 touchdown. Unfortunately, his presence was one of the only notable positives from tonight’s matchup. Bo is BACK 💪 GBvsDEN on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/THCoTwHnA3 — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 Sloppy preseason football: Too many penalties, too many mistakes. The preseason provides an opportunity for NFL teams to work out the kinks. In turn, hopefully gaining some discipline in the process. That didn’t happen tonight for the Broncos who were in many ways their own worst enemies. This was a really sloppy performance and not up to ‘the standard’ the team has set for themselves. Whether it was extending drives for the Packers with third down penalties, turning the ball over or dropped passes on offense, everything after the first two drives seemed problematic for Denver. Penalties were something Broncos struggled with immensely last season. Given such, it is still a bit of a concern seeing that trend continue through two preseason games. They had 10 this evening. Alongside this, I thought the Broncos’ defensive coverage shells were a little vanilla. Yeah, it’s the preseason. I get that, but those cornerbacks were playing off quite a bit too much for my liking. Would've been nice to see the preseason winning streak continue but Sean Payton will absolutely use this loss where the #Broncos made mistakes in all 3 phases as a learning opportunity for the team to keep their focus on the details — Ryan Edwards (@redwardsradio) August 22, 2026 Offensive line depth and run game struggles against Packers The Broncos have a strong starting five on the offensive line. Additionally, versatile swing backup Alex Palczewski is capable of answering the call if need be. Unfortunately, I thought of the backup offensive lineman struggled tonight. Between Calvin Throckmorton and Gavin Ortega at center, the Broncos had a handful of botched snaps and interior pressures missed on delayed blitzes. For the most part, Denver struggled to get a consistent push in the running game as well. Last week they had 162 yards on the ground versus the Atlanta Falcons. Tonight, the offense mustered only 69 rushing yards. Moreover, I thought backup tackle Frank Crum struggled for the second straight week. He had a few penalties and several whiffs tonight in pass protection allowing defenders a straight-line path to backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham. A lot of folks have him penciled in as likely to make the 53-man roster, but I’m not sure he has played up to par in these first two outings. Promising fourth-round rookie Kage Casey looked good last week. Though he didn’t seem to play as well in his second NFL game. I thought he looked less comfortable playing on the right side in the second half and didn’t get much push up front going up against the Packers’ second-team defensive line. Miscellaneous thoughts and observations. It didn’t take long for the referees in tonight’s matchup to cook up some questionable calls. Perhaps it’s my orange and blue colored glasses, but I thought Christian Watson clearly fumbled the ball on the game’s first drive. On Denver’s opening possession on offense, I thought Courtland Sutton’s sideline catch was legit, but the zebras obviously felt otherwise. That was just the beginning. What kind of roughing the passer call was that on Que Robinson in the second quarter? Dane Key getting shoved to the ground and a missed defensive pass interference call right in front of a ref? Wild. I don’t need to write hundreds of words on how bad the refs were tonight. Everybody who watched witnessed their ineptitude. Last week, the Broncos had a few issues on special teams with their field goal unit. This week, the third phase for Denver continued to be an issue. They allowed several long returns on coverage including a 68-yard kickoff return by Pierre Strong. Maybe next week they will play an issue-free game. Earlier I mentioned not being impressed with the Broncos’ offensive line depth’s performance. The same goes for the defensive line. I was hoping to see some quality play from Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim, but neither flashed getting after the quarterback and on multiple occasions, both were blown off the ball or washed out completely in the running game. Those two need to have a rebound performance against the Minnesota Vikings in the preseason finale next Friday.

title: 2026 preseason: Denver Broncos vs. Green Bay Packers final score
summary: The Denver Broncos got what they hoped for from Bo Nix and the offense in their second preseason game against the Green Bay Packers. Nix would lead the team on two drives for 10 points, which ended up being most of the offensive production Denver would enjoy on the night as the Packers would run […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) warms up before a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos got what they hoped for from Bo Nix and the offense in their second preseason game against the Green Bay Packers. Nix would lead the team on two drives for 10 points, which ended up being most of the offensive production Denver would enjoy on the night as the Packers would run up the score handing Denver their first preseason defeat in three seasons. Jarrett Stidham had a very rough go at it in the second and third quarters, which is a big part of how Green Bay was able to stack points in this game. He’ll need to bounce-back and have a strong preseason finale next week. Broncos vs. Packers final score Team 1st 2nd 3rd 4th Final Green Bay Packers 7 16 0 10 33 Denver Broncos 7 3 3 0 13 First Quarter The Packers received the open kickoff and Jordan Love nearly threw an immediate interception with Riley Moss stepping in front of Christian Watson. Instead it was just an incompletion. On the very next play, Pat Surtain was beaten on the slant but drive his fist into the ball to knock it loose where Moss recovered. However, the officiating crew immediately came in and ruled the receiver down by contact. On replay it looked instant on both counts, so tie went to the offense. After a couple of run stuffs, Nik Bonitto was drawn offsides to bring up a third and inches where Bonitto made up for his penalty with a pressure into Love’s face to force the incompletion. On fourth down, Love would find a wide open receiver on a cross for a 20-yard gain with Surtain in coverage to get the Packers into the red zone. They would run like a million plays inside the 20, before finally converting a third and long for a touchdown to cap a 12-play, 66-yard touchdown drive to open th egame. Bo Nix took the field for the first time since January. His highly anticipated returned to the field began with a run for five yards, but then hit Courtland Sutton high outside who toe-tapped an insane catch that was initially ruled incomplete. He was so good that it needed instant replay to confirm, but somehow the officiating crew didn’t see his toes both in bounds with control of the ball. Typical NFL officiating… That must have ticked Nix off, because then he went deep to Jaylen Waddle for a big 35-yard gain into Packers territory. Three plays later on a third and six, Nix found RJ Harvey on a wheel route for a 21-yard touchdown strike to tie the game right back up. Bo Nix went 3/5 for 60 yards and touchdown on the drive. Love’s night would be done after that opening drive bringing in Tyrod Taylor at quarterback for the Packers’ second drive of the game. Denver’s first-team defense would dispatch that drive quite easily and quickly to give the ball back to Nix and the offense. Rookie Jonah Coleman ripped off a five yard run on the first play, then Nix hit Adam Trautman outside get near the first down where a fullback dive would pick up the first down. The next first down came on an out route to Lil’Jordan Humphrey for 14-yards. The first quarter would end after a few miscues and a penalty by Denver who would face a third and 18 on the other side. Broncos 7, Packers 7. Second Quarter The Broncos would add a field goal to close out their second drive, which ended Bo Nix’s night. He would finish 6/9 for 76 yards and a touchdown. Special teams for Denver was not-so-special on the kickoff giving up a 68-yard return. Pierre Strong Jr. with a 68-yard kick return 🔥 GBvsDEN on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QpchpKwmr0 — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 Fortunately, the Broncos defense stood tall and held the Packers to a mere field goal to tie the game up. The special teams struck back on the next kick return with Kolbe Katsis streaking down the field for a 40-yard return to set Jarrett Stidham up with good field position. Stiddy would leave the offense to a quick three-and-out though. An officiating-assisted drive by the Packers ate up the clock late in the second quarter getting them all the way down inside the 10 yard line. On a third and goal from the two, Tyrod Taylor hit a wide receiver on the sidelines for a touchdown. The Packers would add another field goal late. Stiddy would then throw an immediate interception to give the Packers another field goal after that. Packers 23, Broncos 10. Third Quarter Denver’s offense under Stidham continued to be, well, offensive into the second half. They would quickly punt it away. Que Robinson would make sure Denver got the ball right back with a third down sack on the ensuing Packers’ drive. Que Robinson SACK! pic.twitter.com/LA3ch1ody4 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 22, 2026 Stidham got another series to try to break out of the slump he’d been in all game and it looked like the drive would be killed by a holding call. He got most of the yards back in back-to-back dump offs to McLaughlin, before finding an open receiver on third and 11 for the first down to midfield. The drive would stall again inside field goal range. Payton would decide to go for it on fourth and four where Stiddy would scramble for the first down. That would be it, though, as Denver would settle for a Wil Lutz field goal with less than a minute left in the third. Packers 23, Broncos 13. Fourth Quarter Green Bay’s third team asserted itself to start the fourth quarter with a big gain across midfield that kick started their drive that would result in a game-clinching touchdown. With Sam Ehlinger finally getting his chance to play well into the fourth, he hit rookie tight end Justin Joly for a nice gain out to midfield. The drive would falter from there after Ehlinger would take a pretty ugly sack on third down to bring out the punt unit. The Packers would add one more field goal and that would be it for preseason game number two. Okay, I'm ready for Week 1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 22, 2026 Packers 33, Broncos 13.

title: Broncos vs. Packers: 3 storylines to watch for in Week 2 of NFL preseason
summary: Tue Denver Broncos host the Green Bay Packers tonight for their second preseason game. After a decisive win against the preseason opener against the Atlanta Falcons, the Broncos are looking to continue their success in front of a hometown crowd. Here are three storylines to watch this evening. The return of Bo Nix Quarterback Bo […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 7: Offensive pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos celebrates with quarterback Bo Nix #10 after he threw a touchdown during the second quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Empower Field at Mile High on September 7, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tue Denver Broncos host the Green Bay Packers tonight for their second preseason game. After a decisive win against the preseason opener against the Atlanta Falcons, the Broncos are looking to continue their success in front of a hometown crowd. Here are three storylines to watch this evening. The return of Bo Nix Quarterback Bo Nix starting his first game since the AFC Divisional Playoff matchup versus the Buffalo Bills highlights my storylines to watch. Earlier in the week, Head Coach Sean Payton mentioned Nix will be on a pitch-count—roughly around fourteen plays. That’s not a large sample size, but I’m still excited to see how he operates with Offensive Davis Webb calling the plays. With several new teammates on the offensive side of the ball, Nix should be in store for his best season yet in Year 3. It’s easily the most talented bunch the franchise has had in a decade. Perhaps tonight we will witness some of the early visions Webb has for the offense with Nix leading the way. One thing in particular I’m wondering about: Will we see more of Nix under center? A healthy majority of his snaps to date have been from shotgun. In order for him to make a jump this year, I would like to see some variance and balance with this. Getting under center more would help the Broncos’ run game but also help with having a more explosive play action passing game. Will we see more involvement from tight ends in the passing game? Speaking of quarterbacks, Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger combined for 29 passing attempts in the preseason opener. However, only five throws went to tight ends. Evan Engram was the recipient of three with Lucas Krull and Justin Joly earning the other two. The Broncos have a bunch of young skill positions players. That makes it hard to give everyone equal opportunities in the passing game. Even so, I would like to see more involvement from the tight ends tonight against the Packers. Two players I’m hoping to see get some looks are Joly and fellow rookie Dallen Bentley. Earlier in the week, Engram spoke highly of the rookie tight end duo. Both Joly and Bentley flashed in their final seasons in college and were incredibly productive. It would be nice for them to get some targets. Joly had a penchant for moving the chains and coming down with contested catches at NC State. Bentley was a redzone monster and has the potential to be a difference maker there. Why not dial up some play calls that highlight their strengths? Who can step up to be the fifth man in Denver’s defensive line rotation? The defensive line is one of the big strengths of the Broncos’ defense. D.J. Jones, Zach Allen, Malcolm Roach, and Eyioma Uwazurike have the potential to be a dominant core four in 2026. Though I’m wondering is who will step up and be that key fifth player in the rotation up front. With John Franklin-Myers leaving in free agency there are quite a few snaps up for grabs. The two obvious candidates to take over for some of them are second-year player Sai’vion Jones and rookie Tyler Onyedim. Both were third round picks and developmental prospects that have the traits and talent to eventually become starters in the NFL. Unfortunately, that possibility seems further down the road than one would hope. I wasn’t too impressed with either last week against the Falcons. Despite getting a lot of praise and hype through training camp with some big plays, Onyedim was relatively quiet in his NFL debut. The same can be said for Jones, who notched only one tackle in his reps last Friday. The Broncos will likely dress just five defensive lineman each week of the regular season. That’s why I’m eager to see if one of them can cement themselves as the clear-cut favorite in that battle. If not, we are likely entering a scenario of weekly “Guess Who?” as to who will be active or not. It’s a tough position to make an impact in going from the college to pros, but I’m hoping that one of them can gain some steam in the final two preseason games. Broncos Country, what do you think? What are some things you are looking for in tonight’s matchup versus the Packers? Sound off in the comments section and let me know your thoughts.

title: All eyes on Lions’ offensive line heading into Commanders preseason game
summary: Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook, and asked Detroit Lions fans: Which group will you be watching most closely in the Lions vs. Commanders game? For this week’s survey, we gave fans five groups to choose from to answer our question: Offensive skill players, […]
full_text: From left, Detroit Lions offensive lineman Larry Borom (79). guard Michael Niese (62), offensive lineman Juice Scruggs (70), and guard Miles Frazier (71) practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Tuesday, June 16, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans: Which group will you be watching most closely in the Lions vs. Commanders game? For this week’s survey, we gave fans five groups to choose from to answer our question: Offensive skill players, offensive line, defensive line, linebackers, and secondary. While each group got some attention, one group overwhelmingly received the most fan votes. It’s not surprising that fans landed on the offensive line in this survey, because while each of the above groups still has some unsettled questions, many have been answered as training camp has progressed, while the offensive line seems to have even more unknowns. The left guard competition may be settled, as the Lions appear to be sticking with Christian Mahogany. But is that because he won the job, or because Ben Bartch can’t stay healthy , Miles Frazier has shifted to a swing role, and Juice Scruggs is now needed at center? Scruggs seems like he’s in the lead for the temporary center role—while starter Cade Mays recovers from a broken wrist—but how much better is he than Seth McLaughlin? Also, has Scruggs fully recovered from the recent soft-tissue injury that kept him out of the Lions’ first preseason game? Additionally, we’re expecting to see the Lions’ starting offensive line play in this game—including Mahogany at left guard and Scruggs at center—but that is also because they need to work on their communication. Let’s take a closer look at the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for their selection (lightly edited for clarity). UpAllNight : “The success of this season hinges on the O-Line, and it’s far from settled, particularly at the pivot. Can Seth rise up to the challenge, or will Juice, the seasoned vet, be the better option?” Lee County Flydog : “This team will go as far as the Offense takes them. They have excellent players at the skill positions. Therefore, the OL is the key to their success.” Panzer1943 : “The O-line. This team runs (no pun intended) through that position group. It “should” be better this year. Time will tell, obviously.“ sprtn66 : “I’m more worried of the OL and will be watching as much as I can. The fact that none of the starters are playing next to who they did last season scares me. Cohesion is so important there.” Tappy : “In the end, I think this team wins and loses based on the performance of the offensive line, so that’s what I’m most interested in.” As a reminder, this survey was sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed as +1900 to win this year’s Super Bowl, +900 to win the NFC Championship, and +150 to win the NFC North as the current favorites. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Detroit Lions fans and fans across the country. If you want to receive these surveys by email weekly, you can sign up here .

His status for Saturday afternoon’s preseason game is to be determined, per Miller. It’s a relief for both Rakestraw and the Lions. During Thursday’s […]
full_text: Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co More good injury news for the Detroit Lions. According to Fox 2 Detroit’s Dan Miller, cornerback Ennis Rakestraw—who left Thursday’s practice early—only has an ankle injury that is not considered serious. His status for Saturday afternoon’s preseason game is to be determined, per Miller. It’s a relief for both Rakestraw and the Lions. During Thursday’s practice, Rakestraw went down on his own while shifting directions, and he had to hobble over to the sidelines on his own. After being tended to by trainers for several minutes, he was able to walk off the field under his own power, albeit gingerly. Rakestraw has been in competition for both a starting outside cornerback and nickel job, and while his training camp got off to a rough start, he had just started to put together some strong practices. The news is also good for the Lions because their cornerback room has been relatively thin since they decided to cut Terrion Arnold amidst his legal troubles. Right now, that room consists of projected starter D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin, with Rakestraw, Nick Whiteside, Roger McCreary, rookie Keith Abney and Khalil Dorsey to round out the room. With the Lions only having a walkthrough on Friday, the next time we’ll hear directly from the coaching staff is after Saturday’s preseason game against the Washington Commanders, which kicks off at 12 p.m. ET.

full_text: For the first time in 2026, your Detroit Lions are back inside the friendly confines of Ford Field, playing in their second preseason game of the year as they host the Washington Commanders. There were plenty of positives and negatives from last week’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals, with this week’s game against Washington being another opportunity for players to leave their mark on the coaching staff ahead of cut-down day. In case you missed it, myself and my good friend, Meko Scott, broke down several players that have a lot to lose/gain this week against Washington over on the Pride of Detroit YouTube Channel. Lions coach Dan Campbell has already mentioned that we will see some starters against the Commanders, although we still don’t know the details as far as which will be in pads, and which will be in street clothes. That is, other than quarterback Jared Goff, who Campbell was clear about not playing during his Thursday morning media availability. With that said, we should get a good look at portions of what figures to be the starting offensive line on Saturday. That leads us perfectly into today’s question of the day — what are you hoping to see in the Lions’ second preseason game against the Commanders? My answer: I would really like it if we could come away from this game with a few more answers surrounding the offensive line. If I were a betting man, I would guess that we will see every starter not named Penei Sewell for at least a few series on Saturday. Can either Juice Scruggs or Seth McLaughlin do enough to convince this coaching staff that they can fill in at center until Cade Mays returns later this season? What about you? title: 4 roster hints left by Detroit Lions ST coordinator Dave Fipp
summary: In just over a week, the Detroit Lions will have to reduce their roster total from 90 players to 53. It’s a devastating day for players, and a tough one for front offices who often agonize over the final few roster spots. Through training camp practices and preseason performances, we do our best to try […]
full_text: Lions special teams coordinator Dave Fipp speaks to the media before the organized team activities in Allen Park on Thursday, May 23, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In just over a week, the Detroit Lions will have to reduce their roster total from 90 players to 53. It’s a devastating day for players, and a tough one for front offices who often agonize over the final few roster spots. Through training camp practices and preseason performances, we do our best to try and predict what that roster may end up looking like, but there’s one more piece to that puzzle. Sometimes the coaching staff lays out the picture right there in front of you. Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp doesn’t have the power to cut players. Those decisions are above his pay grade. But he holds a pretty important part to the evaluation process. For the last few spots on the 53-man roster, it’s often special teams skills that will tip the scales in one direction or another. So Fipp’s evaluation in that phase is critical during the cut-down phase. On Wednesday, Fipp talked to the media to offer his thoughts on training camp. Here are four hints he may have dropped about how the team will trim their roster on Aug. 30. You can’t just be a good special teamer One of Fipp’s first comments that turned my head was his thoughts on the evolution on the league. No longer can players just win a role by being a decent special teamer. Teams need to be able to trust you on offense or defense. “We’ve had more injuries collectively, probably as a league. You’re playing more players throughout the course of a year. I tell the players now, ‘You’re going to make the team probably in two phases. You’re going to have to play on offense and special teams or defense and special teams.’ And I know this, the more that you can do, the better in modern football,” Fipp said. What does it mean for the roster? This is likely why we’ve seen someone like wide receiver Tay Martin starting to get first-team reps on offense. The Lions have seen him thrive on special teams. But could he hold up if Detroit needed him in a pinch as a receiver? You may think this quote could put someone like Sione Vaki or Khalil Dorsey in danger—two players who are considered elite special teamers, but haven’t shown much on their respective side of the ball yet. However, Fipp did offer a caveat. “If all you can do is play on special teams, you’re going to have to be really, really special to make it just on that,” Fipp said. I would consider both Vaki and Dorsey pretty special on special teams—not to mention that both Vaki and Dorsey have sprinkled in with the first teamers here and there. Linebackers are valued highly on special teams Fipp was asked about Ahmed Hassanein’s value on special teams, and he gave an interesting answer. Basically, he said that defensive linemen—while used a little on kickoffs—are put in a tough spot on special teams. They’re so used to playing in tight areas on defense that the openness of special teams can prove difficult. Linebackers, however, are quite used to playing in space, playing fast, and playing physical, and Fipp pointed to that group specifically as one that has to contribute on special teams significantly. And per Fipp, that group has stood out: “Like linebacker, there’s four guys probably. You’ve got Erick Hunter, you’ve got (Joe) Bachie, you’ve got (Troy) Reeder and you’ve got (Amen) Ogbongbemiga. These four players, they can all play. You’ve got Erick) Hunter, the young guy, the other guys have all played in the league and it’s very, very competitive,” Fipp said. What it means for the roster: I think your roster predictions should have at least six linebackers, maybe seven. Beyond Fipp talking about how important and competitive the room is, consider this: on Thursday Dan Campbell said they want to pull back Jack Campbell’s special teams snaps because of how valuable he is on defense. Now look at this punt coverage team from last year: That’s four linebackers just on one punt team. And with Jimmy Rolder potentially coming back instead of getting placed on injured reserve, it could force the Lions to go heavy on linebacker early. No rookies on punt teams? Lions undrafted rookie Erick Hunter is one of the most intriguing depth players on the roster. By Fipp’s own admission, he’s been making plays daily on special teams. But Fipp was also quick to point out the mistakes he’s making. “He’s definitely done something probably every practice where you’re like, ‘Wow, he did a great job there.’ Or he stood out, and that’s really what you’re looking for. Now that being said, he’s also made some big mistakes too. And it’s like, ‘Man, how much of that can you weather?’” Fipp said. That prompted Fipp to tell a story about his favorite coach of all time: Bill Belichick. Apparently the former Patriots coach had a policy where he wouldn’t play rookies on punt team because the cost of a mental error in that phase could have a devastating impact on the game. “He just didn’t want that to happen because he knew a mistake in that phase is devastating,” Fipp said. “So anytime you have to put a young player out there like that, you have got to be careful. And that’s [Hunter’s] challenge that he’s fighting the other guys have experience, but they haven’t in some ways flashed as much as he has at certain things too. So, it’ll be interesting.” What it means for the roster: It certainly seems like the Lions may play things a bit safe when it comes to their linebacker depth. Someone like Hunter undoubtedly provides some upside and promise, but if he can’t clean up some of the mental errors, it sounds like Fipp wouldn’t risk putting him out there. Maybe they’d be more comfortable letting him develop on the practice squad first, but there’s never a guarantee he makes it there. Return man candidates First of all, Fipp was very direct in talking about the punt return competition, basically calling it a two-man race. “You have the returner position with (Tom) Kennedy and (Greg) Dortch really at punt returner,” Fipp said. “(Dominic) Lovett fitting into that a little bit, but really probably Kennedy and Dortch right now in my opinion.” What it means for the roster: Well, that’s certainly a strike against Lovett, who is very much on the roster bubble. He’ll have to find an impact on special teams elsewhere. He was a good gunner at Georgia, but he hasn’t been getting many top-team reps there in camp. Additionally, Fipp talked about what he prefers in that kick returner role. “I would like a bigger, stronger guy on kickoff return. And most of that’s just durability,” Fipp said. “I mean, those guys take some shots and I would say there’s a little bit more contact with those guys. It’s a little bit more like a run play than it is ball out in space, that’s a little bit more like a punt return.” That explains why Detroit has tried to use bigger running backs and linebackers at the position over speedy, smaller receivers. What it means for the roster: Players like Isiah Pacheco (210 pounds) and Jabari Small (208) fit the description pretty well, while it may be tougher for someone like Jacob Saylors (195) to fit the bill. That said, Saylors has gotten a lot of work there, and Fipp specifically praised the job he did on special teams last year, which included 33 kick returns. “I love Saylors. I loved him a year ago. He came in and really helped us out on special teams,” Fipp said. “And I thought he played very, very well for us on teams a year ago.”

(Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If you’re new here, we track who plays with the first- and second-team offensive and defensive units for the Green Bay Packers throughout the preseason because it’s a much cleaner picture of what the team looks like than the overall snap count. When third-stringers are in the game in the first half, like they were on Friday against the Denver Broncos, things get muddied up a lot more than a regular-season game, where any playing time means a player is being made a priority. Last week, we broke down what the depth chart looked like against the Pittsburgh Steelers . Today, we’re going to compare and contrast what some of the differences are — if there were any — at each position. At the end of the article, after showing our work with the first- and second-team units, we’re going to drop a full depth chart of every position on the team. I hope you enjoy the content. Packers 1st Team Offense Quarterback Jordan Love: 12 snaps Like last week, Jordan Love got one drive in the game. For what it’s worth, head coach Matt LaFleur said that the plan is to play the starters in the team’s joint practice against the Arizona Cardinals (coached by his little brother), and to rest the starters in the final preseason game of 2026. Running Back MarShawn Lloyd: 8 snaps Chris Brooks: 4 snaps With Josh Jacobs (groin) out, MarShawn Lloyd remained the top ball-carrier with the first-team unit. Last week, Lloyd took all nine snaps, while he split a few reps with Chris Brooks, who was inactive last week with a hamstring injury, this time around. Receiver Matthew Golden: 9 snaps Christian Watson: 9 snaps Bo Melton: 4 snaps Skyy Moore: 3 snaps Savion Williams: 2 snaps For the most part, Skyy Moore took up the snaps that Jayden Reed (out with an ankle) would have played this week. To make it simple, it really does seem like the team is treating Moore as Reed’s backup (the slot position), Bo Melton as Matthew Golden’s backup (the X position) and Savion Williams as Christian Watson’s backup (the Z position). That’s all you really need to know here. Tight End Josh Whyle: 12 snaps Drake Dabney: 9 snaps Yes, the Packers played 75 percent of their first-team snaps out of 12 (two-tight end) personnel against Denver. They ran a lot of outside zone and bootlegs on base downs, looking like the early version of the LaFleur offense when he was just a full season removed from being the offensive coordinator for the Los Angeles Rams. Maybe that’s why they’re looking for different bodies/types of players at guard compared to 2025, when they were more of a vertical running game? For what it’s worth, Josh Whyle has played 20 total snaps with the first-team offense through two games, while Drake Dabney has played 12. Whyle and Dabney have moved up the depth chart with Tucker Kraft still getting his feet wet after his ACL tear and Luke Musgrave being on the PUP list with a neck injury. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan: 12 snaps (LT) Jager Burton: 12 snaps (LG) Sean Rhyan: 12 snaps (C) Jacob Monk: 12 snaps (RG) Anthony Belton: 12 snaps (RT) This is the same lineup the Packers used to open up against the Steelers, as left guard Aaron Banks (knee) and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) continue to be held out when the bullets are live. Packers 2nd Team Offense Quarterback Tyrod Taylor: 21 snaps While some might want Kyle McCord to take over as the backup quarterback, it remained the Taylor Show on Friday. He’s taken all 34 snaps with the second-team offense, even if he only has eight completions and 38 yards to show for it. Running Back Chris Brooks: 9 snaps MarShawn Lloyd: 7 snaps Pierre Strong Jr.: 5 snaps MarShawn Lloyd played a couple of early snaps with the second-team offense, like he did last week, before handing it off to the rest of the backs. With Brooks now healthy, he played the most out of the Packers’ top healthy trio. Jaden Nixon, who got three snaps with the second-team offense, received none this week as Brook entered the lineup. Receiver Bo Melton: 18 snaps Isaiah Neyor: 15 snaps Skyy Moore: 8 snaps J. Michael Sturdivant: 7 snaps Will Sheppard: 4 snaps Here’s something interesting: Savion Williams didn’t play with the second-team offense at all. No injury has been reported for him, either. As of now, the team treating him like a starter and sitting him after the first-team unit got shut down is a possibility. Notably, he also didn’t return kicks to start the game — a role he previously played in Week 1. I wouldn’t make too much of Moore receiving fewer snaps than Isaiah Neyor, who stepped in for Williams with the second-teamers today. Moore has been a slot-exclusive player, like Reed, so his playing time is dependent on there not being a second tight end or running back on the field. Last week, when Williams was in the lineup with the 2s, Bo Melton and Williams played 11 snaps each, Moore played 9 in the slot and Neyor played 4 off the bench. It’s nice that J. Michael Sturdivant, who might have left the Broncos game with a concussion, and Will Sheppard were able to get a couple snaps with the second-team offense in this game. Tight End Drake Dabney: 19 snaps Messiah Swinson: 13 snaps So far, Dabney has played 30 snaps with the second-team offense and Messiah Swinson has played 18. These are the team’s fourth and fifth tight ends, when everyone is healthy. The problem: Two guys ahead of them aren’t healthy yet. Offensive Line John Williams: 21 snaps (LT) Jager Burton: 21 snaps (LG) Jacob Monk: 21 snaps (C) Donovan Jennings: 21 snaps (RG) Anthony Belton: 21 snaps (RT) Unlike last week, Jordan Morgan didn’t play snaps as the left tackle with the second-string unit, which pushed John Williams into the lineup. Otherwise, these are the same players who played with Tyrod Taylor under center against the Steelers. Packers 1st Team Defense Defensive Line Karl Brooks: 8 snaps Nazir Stackhouse: 6 snaps Chris McClellan: 6 snaps Jonathan Ford: 4 snaps Devonte Wyatt: 4 snaps Jaden Crumedy: 4 snaps Anthony Campbell: 3 snaps Alright, this one gets weird. The Packers used a starting defensive line of Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks on the ends and Jonathan Ford at nose tackle to start the game, but didn’t use Wyatt after the first drive. They also hardly used Brooks (who was sat with the rest of the starters on the first-team defense) on the first-team defense’s second drive versus Denver. Don’t make too much of this pecking order. Clearly, Nazir Stackhouse, Chris McClellan, Jonathan Ford, Anthony Campbell and Jaden Crumedy are all fighting for playing time. Interestingly, Warren Brinson didn’t play a single snap in this game, despite not being listed as a scratch by the Packers, unlike the other players who didn’t see action. This is also your reminder that Javon Hargrave is still missing preseason games, but returned to practice as he recovers from a knee injury. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness: 10 snaps Barryn Sorrell: 8 snaps Brenton Cox Jr.: 5 snaps Collin Oliver: 2 snaps Nothing is shocking here. This seems to be the pecking order, at least while Micah Parsons (PUP, knee) and Dani Dennis-Sutton (illness) aren’t involved. For what it’s worth, Collin Oliver usually comes on the field on obvious passing situations, but otherwise this is a pretty clear 1-2-3-4 from the team. Off-Ball Linebacker Zaire Franklin: 14 snaps Edgerrin Cooper: 14 snaps These are your starting linebackers. Cornerback Keisean Nixon: 14 snaps Benjamin St-Juste: 8 snaps Brandon Cisse: 6 snaps Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse were the starters tonight, but Cisse dropped out with an injury right before the second defensive drive of the game. After the game, Cisse called the injury “ nothing serious .” Benjamin…

(Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse got the start opposite Keisean Nixon on the outside against the Denver Broncos on Friday, but he only played one of the first-team defense’s two drives in the game after going down with an injury after a punt. According to the Green Bay Press-Gazette ’s Ryan Wood , Cisse said he got double-teamed as a punter gunner and felt “a little something” in his knee after the play. Reporters and fans in attendance in Denver saw Cisse go over to the blue tent while the first-team defense played through their second drive, and Cisse later was photographed riding a stationary bike on the sideline. Michael Sturdivant, who appeared to exit the game with a possible concussion, or defensive lineman Warren Brinson, who surprisingly didn’t get a single snap versus Denver, despite not being listed as a scratch by the team.

title: Green Bay Packers vs. Denver Broncos final score, recap: Trey Smack continues hot start
summary: Coming into tonight’s action, the Green Bay Packers hadn’t won a game since December 7th against the Chicago Bears, as their last trip to Denver started them on a five game-losing streak (six if you want to include the preseason opener) that capped off with the team being sent home by those same Bears in […]
full_text: Aug 21, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) lines up a field kick during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Coming into tonight’s action, the Green Bay Packers hadn’t won a game since December 7th against the Chicago Bears, as their last trip to Denver started them on a five game-losing streak (six if you want to include the preseason opener) that capped off with the team being sent home by those same Bears in the Wild Card round. Tonight, they sort of got that monkey off their back, as they beat the Broncos 33-13 at elevation. Overall, the depth of the team played well on Friday, unlike their Week 1 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, when their fourth-team defense gave up a lead and allowed three touchdowns in a row to end the game. This time, the Packers’ defense (and offense) held strong, despite the Broncos keeping their first- and second-team units in the game significantly longer than Green Bay. The story of the game, and the preseason, continues to be rookie kicker Trey Smack, though. The sixth-round pick went three of three last week, not including a deep field goal that was taken off the board because the Steelers committed a penalty. How would he outdo himself in Week 2? By going four of four (and three of three on PATs), including a 59-yard field goal, one yard longer than his long the previous week. Look at Matt LaFleur’s face after Trey Smack just hit a 59-yard field goal. He’s one of us… 😂 pic.twitter.com/mnUe3VfFwJ — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) August 22, 2026 In the kickoff game, Smack’s kickoffs continue to be placed inside the 10-yard line and near the numbers, the toughest place for returners to bring the ball out from under the NFL’s new “dynamic kickoff” rules. All signs are positive on the rookie in live action. Hopefully, it’ll continue through the regular season. Elsewhere on special teams, fourth-string running back Pierre Strong Jr. busted a 68-yard kickoff return, while receiver Skyy Moore had a nice 16-yard punt return himself. YOOOOOOOOO 📺: Packers TV Network pic.twitter.com/ytx4vBIY8m — Green Bay Packers (@packers) August 22, 2026 On offense, a brewing debate among the Packers faithful is whether or not Kyle McCord, a 2025 draft pick who was signed on a reserve/futures deal, is out-playing backup quarterback Tyrod Taylor. So far this preseason, McCord has completed 24 of 35 passes for 220 yards (6.3 yards per pass) and has orchestrated three successful two-minute drills, including two in the first half on Friday. Meanwhile, Taylor has thrown 16 passes for eight completions and 38 yards (2.8 yards per pass). Here’s a breakdown of how the game flow went tonight: The starting offense played one drive, which lasted 12 plays and went 63 yards for a touchdown as quarterback Jordan Love found running back MarShawn Lloyd on an option route for paydirt. The second-team offense played three drives before McCord got the opportunity for two two-minute drills to end the first half. On the first drive, matched up against the Broncos’ starting defense, the backup offense punted, but they scored a touchdown and a field goal against Denver’s second-team unit. The Packers’ starting defense actually played two drives, with the exception being that Brandon Cisse, who was hurt on special teams between drives, and the starting defensive line were sat for their second look. They allowed a touchdown on their first drive, as safety Xavier McKinney and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper gave up explosives through the air on third down, but held the starting offense (again — minus their starting defensive linemen) to a field goal. The second-team defense played three drives and didn’t allow a single point. In fact, they gave up just 32 yards over three drives. For perspective, the Broncos kept their second-team offense on the field until the early fourth quarter, while the Packers sat their second-unit for the entire second half. On the injury front, all of these players were listed as scratches by Green Bay: RB Josh Jacobs (groin) WR Jayden Reed (ankle) TE Tucker Kraft (knee) TE Luke Musgrave (PUP, neck) LG Aaron Banks (knee) RT Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) OL Darian Kinnard (ankle) DL Javon Hargrave (knee) DL Jordon Riley (PUP, ankle) EDGE Micah Parsons (PUP, knee) EDGE Dani Dennis-Sutton (illness) CB Carrington Valentine (hamstring) S Javon Bullard (foot) LS Matt Orzech (PUP, calf) Virtually everyone not on the PUP list is practicing with the team. Don’t be scared of how long this list looks. The team is just being very conservative with injuries right now. Expect most of these players to be at practice in Green Bay next week. As far as guys making their debuts, defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt, cornerback Kamal Hadden and cornerback Domani Jackson played in their first preseason game of 2026 today. Hadden actually started in the slot role in place of Javon Bullard. Last week, it was safety Kitan Oladapo in the slot. Hadden looked like a noticeable improvement as a slot defender, compared to Oladapo, who has played better as a safety. Interestingly, it doesn’t look like Warren Brinson played a single snap of defense today, despite him not previously being listed with an injury either pre-game or in this week’s set of practices. Stay tuned for an update there. Look for an update on Cisse, too, as we aren’t sure on the specifics of his injury, other than he got hurt on special teams before the second defensive drive and was later seen riding on a stationary bike on the sideline.
